title: Check yourself: The error result, and what the loop does with each kind

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A refund tool meets a slow card service, and each time it answers with the text "Operation failed". The agent tries three more times and then apologises, though a colleague could have settled the case. Which change helps most?

options.text: Raise the attempts from three to ten, with a longer wait between them
options.says: Ruled out because more attempts do not help when the reply gives no reason: "Retry every failed call a few times, whatever the reason".

options.text: Add a prompt rule on retries and a second rule on when to give up
options.says: Ruled out because a model with nothing to go on can only guess: "A model that has to guess will retry a request that can never succeed".

options.text: Reply with a category, a retry flag and a message that says what to do
options.says: The agent can only choose a recovery if the reply says which one applies.

options.text: Return an empty list marked as a success and let the run continue
options.says: Ruled out because an empty success hides the failure: "an empty list marked as a success tells the agent that the search found nothing".

questions.stem: A calendar service gets three requests: one asks for a function that it lacks, one gives a date as "next Friday" where a calendar date is needed, and one reaches a backend that answers 503. Which request alone is a protocol error?

options.text: The one that has nowhere to be routed
options.says: Only a request with nothing to run is a protocol error; the other two reached the tool.

options.text: The one whose date has the wrong format
options.says: Ruled out because "an input validation failure" is a tool execution error, which the model can repair.

options.text: The one that met the busy backend
options.says: Ruled out because a failed backend call is an "API failure" that comes back with the flag and a message that allows "retry with adjusted parameters".

options.text: All three, because each of them ended in a failure
options.says: Ruled out because the specification wants execution errors passed on: "Clients SHOULD provide tool execution errors to language models to enable self-correction."
